subject: variable s can be found in the output

messages.author: 08749fffc5019a54
messages.subject: variable s can be found in the output
parts:
Hi NIMBLE experts,

 

I am trying to use Nimble to construct a HMM model that contains response and response time. I am very surprised by Nimble's running speed, but I encounter some problems: I provide the node name or variable name to monitor, but no information about variable s can be found in the output

Can anyone help me with this problem?

Thanks！

Xu

 

Here is my code,

The Y means response;

The lrt means response time;

The total number of subjects is denoted by n, and the total number of items is denoted by p;

The "s" is a matrix of N*P, which means potential state.

 

library(nimble)

library(readr)

 

HMM_code <- nimbleCode({

  for (i in 1:n){

    for (j in 1:p){

      for (k in 1:K){

        eta.1[i, j, k] <- - beta.1[j, k]

        psum.1[i, j, k] <- sum(eta.1[i, j, 1:k])

        exp.psum.1[i, j, k] <- exp(psum.1[i, j, k])

        prob.1[i, j, k] <- exp.psum.1[i, j, k] / sum(exp.psum.1[i, j, 1:K])

        

        eta.2[i, j, k] <- theta[i] - beta.2[j, k]

        psum.2[i, j, k] <- sum(eta.2[i, j, 1:k])

        exp.psum.2[i, j, k] <- exp(psum.2[i, j, k])

        prob.2[i, j, k] <- exp.psum.2[i, j, k] / sum(exp.psum.2[i, j, 1:K])

        

        prob[i, j, k] <- equals(s[i,j],1)*prob.1[i, j, k] +equals(s[i,j],2)*prob.2[i, j, k]

      }

      Y[i, j] ~ dcat(prob[i, j, 1:K])

    }

    theta[i] ~ dnorm(0,1)

  }

  for (i in 1:n) {

    for (j in 1:p) {

      lrt[i,j]~dnorm(mu_rt[s[i,j],i,j],pr.rt)

      mu_rt[1,i,j] <- icept

      mu_rt[2,i,j] <- icept + icept.star[j]-speed[i] - cor*(pow(theta[i],2) + theta[i])

    }  

  }

  

  for (j in 1:p) {

    beta.1[j,1] <- 0

    for (k in 2:K) {

      beta.1[j, k] ~ dnorm(0, 1)

    }

    

    beta.2[j,1] <- 0

    for (k in 2:K) {

      beta.2[j, k] ~ dnorm(0, 1)

    }

    icept.star[j]  ~ T(dnorm(0,1),0,)

  }

  

  for (i in 1:n) {

    speed[i] ~ dnorm(0,pr.s)

  }

  

  icept ~ dnorm(0,1)

  pr.s ~ dgamma(0.1,0.1)

  pr.rt ~ dgamma(0.1,0.1)

  cor ~ dnorm(0,1)

  

  for (i in 1:n){

    s[i,1] ~ dcat(pi[i,1:2])

    for (j in 2:p){

      s[i,j] ~ dcat(a[i,s[i,j-1],1:2])

    }

  }

  

  pi.alpha[1] <- 1

  pi.alpha[2] <- 1

  

  a1.alpha[1] <- 0.5

  a1.alpha[2] <- 0.5

  

  a2.alpha[1] <- 0.5

  a2.alpha[2] <- 0.5

  

  

  for (i in 1:n){

    a[i,1,1:2] ~ ddirich(a1.alpha[1:2])

    a[i,2,1:2] ~ ddirich(a2.alpha[1:2])

  }

  

  for (i in 1:n){  

    pi[i,1:2] ~ ddirich(pi.alpha[1:2])    

  }

 

})

 

 

Y <- read_csv("C:/Users/x2845/Desktop/600_10_RS.csv")[-1]

lrt <- read_csv("C:/Users/x2845/Desktop/600_10_RT.csv")[-1]

 

Y <- as.matrix(Y)

lrt <- as.matrix(lrt)

 

n <- nrow(Y)

p <- ncol(Y)

K <- 6

 

constants <- list(n=n,p=p,K=K)

 

data <- list(Y=Y,lrt=lrt)

 

set.seed(2)

inits <- list(theta    = rnorm(n, 0, 1),

              s =  matrix(sample(c(1,2), p*n, replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.5, 0.5)),nrow = n)

)

 

monitors = c("beta.1","beta.2", "theta","a","s","pi","cor")

 

hmm_model <- nimbleModel(HMM_code, constants, data, inits)

modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(hmm_model)

cmodel <- compileNimble(hmm_model)

cModelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = hmm_model)

samples <- runMCMC(cModelMCMC, niter = 10000, nburnin = 5000)

sCols <- grep("s", colnames(samples))

samplesSummary(samples[, c(sCols)])

messages.subject: Re: variable s can be found in the output
parts:
Hi Xu,

I think you need to use configureMCMC to build a MCMC configuration object first and then call buildMCMC. For configureMCMC, you can provide monitors as an argument.

mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(hmm_model, monitors = monitors)
modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf) 

-Wei

parts:
Hi Xu,

In addition to what Wei suggests, you can pass the monitors argument directly to buildMCMC, e.g.,

modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(hmm_model, monitors=monitors)

In your code, you forgot to provide monitors as an argument to any of nimble's functions.

-Chris
